values: An invisible inertial field protects one creature for up to 24 hours or until expended. It activates automatically against incoming concentrated physical projectiles traveling approximately 120 km/h or faster relative to the protected creature. The field arrests ordinary projectiles such as arrows, bolts, sling stones, and bullets, redirecting their kinetic energy into the surrounding ground or space. Heavy projectiles, such as cannonballs, exceed the basic shield's stopping capacity. Thrown objects and slow melee attacks usually fall below its activation threshold. Once struck by a projectile it can stop, the shield continues intercepting qualifying projectiles for approximately 0.25 seconds before collapsing. Recasting replaces the existing shield; only the strongest shield effect on a target applies. Shield layers granted by future higher-level upgrades are separate from stacking multiple castings.

Automatically stops ordinary physical projectiles moving at approximately 120 km/h or more relative to the target. Lasts 24 hours or until triggered; protects for approximately 0.25 seconds after activation, then dissipates. Does not stop heavy siege projectiles. Multiple castings do not stack.

An invisible inertial field limits the target creature's downward falling speed to 2 m/s (7.2 km/h) for 30 minutes, allowing safe, convenient descents and gentle landings. The effect operates automatically whenever the target falls, safely reducing the speed of a creature already falling faster than this limit. The target cannot adjust descent speed, hover, or steer using the spell. The target may dismiss Slow Fall at any time, but dismissal ends the spell permanently until recast. Recasting on the same target resets its duration to 30 minutes rather than stacking. If the spell expires or is dismissed in midair, the target resumes accelerating normally under gravity.

Caps downward falling speed at 2 m/s for 30 minutes. Automatic; no steering, hovering, or speed adjustment. Recasting resets duration. Dismissal ends the spell; falling resumes normally if it ends midair.

The caster reinforces a willing creature's resistance to external physical forces without hindering its voluntary movement. For 30 minutes, the target gains a +4 + caster's ATR bonus to checks and saving throws made to resist involuntary physical displacement, including being pushed, pulled, dragged, knocked backward, or knocked prone by an external physical force. The bonus also applies against displacement from strong winds, currents, and similar environmental forces. The spell does not reduce damage, prevent grappling itself, negate gravity, stop magical teleportation, or make the target immovable; sufficiently strong forces can still displace the target. The effect requires no sustain cost and may be dismissed by the target on demand, ending the spell.

+4 + caster's ATR to checks and saving throws against involuntary physical displacement, including push, pull, drag, knockback, and physically induced prone. Lasts 30 minutes without sustain. No damage reduction or absolute anchoring; target may dismiss at will.

The caster sustains an invisible, self-centered field extending 1 m in radius that arrests the propagation of damaging area effects, regardless of damage type or material. When a fireball, breath weapon, cone, line, shockwave, or other damaging area effect encounters the field, the first hex affected within the field takes its normal effect, but the effect cannot propagate farther into protected hexes. If an area effect originates inside the field, its initial affected hex is still affected, but it cannot spread to additional protected hexes. Thus, dragon breath approaching from outside dissipates at the leading edge before reaching the caster, whereas breath originating directly in the caster's hex can still damage the caster. The field suppresses friendly and hostile AoE propagation alike. It does not reduce direct damage in the first affected hex, stop single-target attacks, or remove environmental hazards already present. The field moves with the caster and remains active only while sustained.

Sustained self-centered 1 m radius field. Damaging AoEs of any type affect only the first hex they reach within the field; propagation to further protected hexes stops. Effects originating within the field affect their initial hex only. Works on friendly and hostile effects. No protection against direct attacks or existing hazards.

The caster imposes an inertial restriction on one creature, limiting its maximum rate of movement for ATR rounds. An unwilling target may resist with a Fortitude saving throw; a willing target may forgo the save. The target cannot move more than 5 m per AP, regardless of movement type, direction, or bonuses. This restriction applies to movement from any source, not only voluntary Move actions. Movement that would otherwise be 5 m per AP or less is unaffected.
The target's movement is capped at 5 m per AP for ATR rounds, regardless of movement type or bonuses. An unwilling target gets a Fortitude save; a willing target may forgo it. No sustain.

The caster enchants one object, fixing it in place relative to its surroundings for ATR minutes. To establish the enchantment, the caster must maintain uninterrupted physical contact with the object for 6 seconds while holding it stationary. The enchanted object resists displacement with force equivalent to 100 times its own weight, up to a maximum of 100 kg of force (the weight of a 100 kg mass). The enchantment does not increase the object's actual mass or durability. When a force greater than its resistance is applied, the enchantment yields and the object can move; when the force drops below the threshold, it immediately becomes stationary again at its new position. Exceeding the threshold does not end the spell. No saving throw is granted. The effect expires after ATR minutes and requires no sustain.

After 6 seconds of uninterrupted touch while stationary, one object remains fixed in place for ATR minutes. Resists displacement up to 100× its own weight, capped at 100 kg equivalent. Greater force moves it; it reanchors when that force ceases. Does not increase mass or durability. No save or sustain.

The caster places one conscious, willing living creature into stasis. The target must be capable of knowingly accepting the spell; unconscious creatures cannot be targeted, and non-sapient creatures require sufficient intelligence to willingly accept its effect. The caster chooses a duration of up to ATR hours when casting. The creature and a thin envelope of surrounding air become locked in a static state: the occupant cannot move, act, perceive, breathe, metabolize, age, or experience the passage of time until released. A smooth, opaque, closely conforming ovoid forms around the creature's posture, enclosing the immobilized air. The cocoon is rigid but movable as a whole; it can be picked up, carried, or transported, while its contents remain fixed relative to one another. The cocoon grants DR 100 against damage. At casting, the caster chooses whether to leave an accessible magical button that can be pressed to terminate stasis early, or to create no button. With no button, the effect lasts until the chosen duration expires unless otherwise dispelled. When stasis ends, the creature resumes normal activity. No sustain cost.

Conscious, knowingly willing living creature enters a movable, opaque ovoid of complete stasis (DR 100) for a caster-set duration up to ATR hours. No action, perception, metabolism, aging, or passage of subjective time. Optional magical button releases early; otherwise expires at the chosen time. No save or sustain.

The caster surrounds one willing creature with an inertial field that spreads the force of physical impacts across a larger area, reducing concentrated injury. For 24 hours, the target has DR 5 against physical attacks, with a pool of 10 damage that can be prevented in total. Each point of damage prevented reduces the remaining pool by 1. When the pool is depleted, the spell collapses. Recasting this spell on the target restores its pool to the maximum of 10 and renews its 24-hour duration; multiple castings do not stack or increase the maximum. This spell does not restore existing injuries.

For 24 hours, a willing creature gains DR 5 vs. physical attacks, up to 10 total damage prevented. Prevention consumes the pool point for point; the effect collapses at 0. Recasting refills the pool and renews the duration, but cannot stack. No healing.

The caster establishes an inertial tether linking themselves to one creature within 5 m. For ATR hours, both participants resist movement that would change the distance separating them; moving without changing their separation is unaffected. The tether begins at strength 10 and imposes a movement-speed penalty in meters equal to its remaining strength whenever either participant spends an AP moving in a way that would change their separation. For each such movement AP, that participant may make a Strength check against DC 10 + cast level + caster's ATR. Each point by which the result exceeds the DC permanently reduces the tether's shared strength by 1 (minimum 0); failed checks do not restore its strength. Apply this reduction before calculating the movement allowed for that AP; the resulting penalty may reduce distance-changing movement to 0 m. Both participants always use the same remaining tether strength, regardless of who weakened it. The tether breaks when its strength reaches 0 or its duration expires. It cannot otherwise be dismissed voluntarily, and a participant's death does not end it. The 5 m range is required only when casting; it does not limit later separation. No saving throw and no sustain cost.

Caster and one creature are tethered for ATR hours (initial strength 10). Both take a movement penalty equal to remaining tether strength in meters when changing their distance apart. Each movement AP permits STR vs. DC 10 + cast level + caster's ATR; excess success permanently lowers shared strength by that amount, applied before movement. Ends at strength 0 or duration expiry, not on death. No save; no voluntary dismissal before Level 6.
Spell can be dismissed at will by the caster.

The caster causes one melee weapon weighing no more than 4 kg to float under their control. When not attacking, the weapon remains within the caster's hex or an adjacent hex. It may temporarily move outward to make a normal melee attack, then immediately returns. The weapon does not attack autonomously. The caster expends the weapon's normal AP cost to attack, substituting ATR for STR + DEX in both attack and damage calculations. The weapon's normal reach increases by 3 m. It cannot perform special attacks. The caster's hands remain free and may be used normally. The caster may transfer the spell to another eligible melee weapon within their hex or an adjacent hex for 1 AP. A creature grabbing, grappling, or otherwise physically impeding the weapon may attempt a Reflex check against DC 10 + caster Level + ATR. On success, the spell ends and the creature takes possession of the weapon.

Float and control one melee weapon of up to 4 kg. Make normal melee attacks using ATR instead of STR + DEX for attack and damage, with +3 m reach. Attacks cost normal AP. No special attacks. Switch weapons for 1 AP. A successful Reflex check against DC 10 + Level + ATR when grabbing or impeding the weapon ends the spell and grants possession.

The caster uses a brief telekinetic impulse to propel themselves through a jump of up to ATR metres, either vertically or horizontally. The spell also assists with the landing, cushioning the descent and preventing falling damage caused by the jump itself. The caster must begin the jump from a supporting surface; it cannot be recast while airborne to extend the jump or simulate flight. The spell does not protect against unrelated falls or additional drops.
Jump up to ATR m vertically or horizontally and land safely from the jump. Must launch from a supporting surface; cannot repeat the jump while airborne.

The caster directs a burst of telekinetic force at one creature within 10 m, pushing it directly away from the spell's origin. The target makes a STR resistance check (d20 + Level + STR + applicable modifiers) against DC 10 + caster Level + ATR, adjusted for relative size. For purposes of the size modifier, the spell acts as a Medium creature regardless of the caster's actual size; apply +4 to the DC for each size category the spell is larger than the target, or -4 for each category it is smaller. Other applicable stability modifiers, including a quadruped's +4 bonus when properly braced, apply to the target's resistance check. On a failed check, the target moves 3 m away from the caster, plus another 3 m for every full 5 points by which the check fails. A failure by 10 or more also knocks the target Prone. If this movement drives the target into a solid obstruction that stops the movement, it takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage, once per casting regardless of the margin of failure. This is primarily a battlefield-control spell, not a damage spell.

STR check vs. spell DC (10 + Level + ATR), with the spell counting as Medium for relative-size modifiers. Failure: push 3 m + 3 m per full 5 points of failure; failure by 10+: also Prone. If stopped by a solid obstruction, deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage once, regardless of failure margin.

For up to 24 hours after casting, the caster holds magical guidance ready to apply to one of their own standard physical ranged weapon attacks (such as an arrow, bolt, or thrown weapon). When making an eligible attack, the caster voluntarily chooses whether to expend the spell. If used, the attack gains +10 to its attack roll provided the target is within the caster's line of sight and no more than 50 m away. The magic guides the projectile during its direct flight but cannot curve it around corners, bypass intervening obstructions, or guide it beyond 50 m from the caster. The weapon's ordinary range, damage, ammunition statistics, and other attack rules remain unchanged. This spell cannot enhance attacks made by other creatures or special attacks at level 1. The caster may make ordinary ranged attacks without using the held spell; doing so does not consume it. The spell ends when voluntarily dismissed, expended on one eligible attack, or after 24 hours, whichever comes first. Only one instance of Guided Projectile can be held at a time. Casting it again while a previous instance is active refreshes that instance's 24-hour duration but does not grant an additional guided attack.

Self only; hold for up to 24 hours. Voluntarily expend on one of your own standard physical ranged weapon attacks: +10 to hit against a target within line of sight and 50 m. No special attacks, no curved shots; normal weapon and ammunition damage/range. Unassisted attacks do not expend the spell. Ends when used, dismissed, or expired. Recasting refreshes the 24-hour duration of the existing instance; does not stack or grant additional uses.

The caster abruptly accelerates one loose, discrete object weighing no more than 1 kg, located within 10 m of the caster, toward a target no more than 10 m from the object's starting position. The object launches at approximately 50 km/h. Make a ranged attack using the caster's ATR. On a hit, the object deals 1d4 damage, regardless of mass; its nature determines whether the damage is bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. Armor penetration is 0 by default. The caster supplies an initial impulse only: after launch, the object follows an ordinary unguided trajectory and cannot turn, correct course, or bypass obstacles. Ordinary gravity and physical obstructions apply. The spell does not make the object structurally stronger: fragile projectiles may break on impact. This spell is intended to weaponize improvised objects rather than replace conventional ranged weaponry.

Choose one loose object up to 1 kg within 10 m. Launch it at ~50 km/h toward a target within 10 m of the object. Ranged attack (ATR); hit deals 1d4 damage, type according to object, armor penetration 0 by default. Unguided after launch; no course correction. Object retains ordinary fragility.

The caster can telekinetically exert up to 5 kgf (approximately 49 N) on one object at a time within 5 m. The force can lift objects weighing up to roughly 5 kg under normal gravity, or move heavier objects when the force needed is sufficiently low. Controlled objects can be moved or manipulated at up to 1 m per second. The caster may release an object and manipulate a different object within range without recasting, but cannot manipulate multiple objects simultaneously. In combat, manipulating an object or performing a discrete interaction costs 1 AP; changing objects adds no separate casting cost. The motion is too slow to make a direct attack or deliver a damaging strike, but the caster may operate accessible physical mechanisms or release a lifted object so that ordinary gravity and other physical forces take effect. The spell provides no tactile feedback.

Sustained: exert up to 5 kgf (~49 N) within 5 m; move/manipulate one object at a time at up to 1 m/s. May switch objects without recasting. In combat, 1 AP per object manipulation/discrete interaction. Cannot make direct attacks using the spell's motion; released objects follow normal physics. No tactile feedback.

The caster releases a concentrated impulse of kinetic force toward one creature within range. The force strikes directly, without requiring a physical projectile or an existing object. At level 1, it delivers a straightforward physical impact without additional effects or forced movement.
Make one ranged attack against a creature within 50 m. On a successful hit, deal 1d4 + ATR bludgeoning damage. No additional effects or forced movement at level 1.

The caster unleashes a concentrated surge of kinetic force across a small area, striking creatures with sudden blunt impacts. Rather than throwing targets back, the abrupt impulse can stagger their movement.

Target one hex within 50 m and make the standard tile-targeting attack. On a successful hit, the Burst affects 4 hexes. Creatures in the area may spend RP to attempt the standard DEX evasion; a successful evasion avoids the Burst entirely. Otherwise, each affected creature takes 1d4 + ATR bludgeoning damage and makes a standard Fortitude save. A failed Fortitude save also makes the creature Staggered for its next turn (no more than one Move action; cannot Run). A successful Fortitude save prevents Staggered but not the damage.

A wave of concentrated kinetic force erupts outward from the caster, striking enemies within 2 m while leaving allies unaffected. Enemies that are struck suffer a blunt impact and may be hurled away from the caster. Where two outward hexes offer equally valid paths for forced movement, the caster chooses the path.

Affect enemies within 2 m of the caster (excluding the caster and allies). Each enemy may spend RP to attempt the standard Wave DEX evasion; success avoids all effects. Otherwise, the enemy takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage, then makes the STR resistance check used by Kinetic Push: d20 + Level + STR + applicable modifiers vs. DC 10 + caster Level + ATR. The spell counts as Medium for relative-size modifiers (+4 DC per category the spell is larger, -4 per category smaller); applicable stability bonuses, including +4 for a braced quadruped, apply. On a failed check, push the enemy directly away from the caster by 3 m, plus 3 m for every full 5 points of failure. Failure by 10 or more also knocks the enemy Prone. If two outward hexes are equally valid, the caster chooses which is entered. If a solid obstruction stops the forced movement, the enemy takes an additional 1d6 bludgeoning damage, once per casting. A successful STR check prevents displacement and Prone, but not the Wave's initial damage.

The caster sustains a controlled kinetic acceleration that increases a willing creature's ground movement speed. The additional motion is supplied by magic, but the creature's physical stamina and resistance to exertion are unchanged. The spell may be maintained while the target remains within 1 km of the caster.

One willing creature touched gains +10 m to its ground movement distance per Move action. Run uses the increased Move distance (4× enhanced movement for the 3 AP Run action). This spell does not grant extra AP, improve endurance, reduce exertion or fatigue, or increase swimming, climbing, or flying movement. Sustain cost 1; the effect ends if the target moves beyond 1 km of the caster.

The caster surrounds a willing creature with a sustained field of kinetic force that diverts incoming physical projectiles, making accurate ranged attacks exceptionally difficult. The shield redirects projectiles rather than stopping all attacks, and remains effective only while sustained within 50 m of the caster.

Ranged attacks that use physical projectiles take a -10 penalty to their attack rolls against the protected creature. This includes arrows, thrown weapons, and other physical projectiles, whether launched mundanely or magically (such as Kinetic Shot). The shield does not hinder melee attacks, projectile-less effects (such as Kinetic Bolt), or area effects that do not make a physical-projectile attack roll against the protected creature. The penalty applies to every qualifying attack while the spell is sustained. Sustain cost: 2. The spell ends if the target moves beyond 50 m of the caster.

The caster causes one ranged weapon weighing no more than 4 kg to float under their control. When not attacking, the weapon remains within the caster's hex or an adjacent hex. The spell operates the weapon's moving parts to aim, ready, load, and fire it, using ordinary ammunition and the weapon's normal attack and reload requirements; it does not create ammunition or grant free reloads. The weapon does not attack autonomously. The caster expends the weapon's normal AP costs and substitutes ATR for STR + DEX in both attack and damage calculations. Attacks use the weapon's normal range and ammunition. The weapon cannot perform special attacks. The caster's hands remain free and may be used normally. The caster may transfer the spell to another eligible ranged weapon within their hex or an adjacent hex for 1 AP. A creature grabbing, grappling, or otherwise physically impeding the weapon may attempt a Reflex check against DC 10 + caster Level + ATR. On success, the spell ends and the creature takes possession of the weapon.

Float and control one ranged weapon of up to 4 kg. Make normal ranged attacks using ATR instead of STR + DEX for attack and damage. Attacks and loading use the weapon's normal AP costs, range, and physical ammunition; no ammunition is created. No special attacks or autonomous attacks. Switch to another eligible ranged weapon for 1 AP. A successful Reflex check against DC 10 + caster Level + ATR when grabbing or impeding the weapon ends the spell and grants possession. Sustain cost: 1.

The caster causes one shield weighing no more than 4 kg to float under their control, hovering in the caster's hex or an adjacent hex and moving with them to provide protection. The shield grants its normal AC bonus as if wielded while leaving the caster's hands free. The shield also compensates for the first enemy by which the caster is outnumbered, nullifying the first -2 AC penalty from flanking. Further outnumbering penalties apply normally. The shield's AC bonus does not stack with another shield's AC bonus. The caster may transfer the spell to another eligible shield in their hex or an adjacent hex for 1 AP. A creature grabbing, grappling, or otherwise physically impeding the shield may attempt a Reflex check against DC 10 + caster Level + ATR. On success, the spell ends and the creature takes possession of the shield.

Float and control one shield of up to 4 kg within the caster's hex or an adjacent hex. Gain the shield's normal AC bonus while keeping both hands free; shield AC bonuses do not stack. Nullify up to the first -2 AC of the penalty caused by being outnumbered (one excess enemy); additional -2 penalties apply as normal. No AP or designated attacker is needed for this flanking protection. Switch shields for 1 AP. A successful Reflex check against DC 10 + caster Level + ATR to grab or impede the shield ends the spell and grants possession. Sustain cost: 1.

Provoke alters a creature's perception of the caster, making the caster the focus of its hostile attention. The target must be able to see the caster when the spell is cast and must remain able to see the caster for the effect to continue. At the beginning of each affected turn, the target makes a Will save against DC 10 + the caster's Level + ATR + modifiers. On a successful save, Provoke ends before the target acts. On a failed save, any hostile action the target takes during that turn must target the caster. Provoke does not require the target to take hostile actions; it may move, heal, assist allies, use items, or take other non-hostile actions normally. The target retains control over how it attacks the caster. An area effect satisfies Provoke if the caster is included among its targets. If the target can no longer see the caster, Provoke ends immediately. Reapplying Provoke refreshes its duration rather than creating multiple instances.

For up to ATR of the target's turns, any hostile action taken by the target must target the caster. At the beginning of each affected turn, the target makes a Will save to end Provoke before acting. Provoke ends immediately if the target can no longer see the caster.

Overlook suppresses the caster's visual salience, causing nearby creatures to see the caster without readily giving them meaningful attention. While the spell is sustained, when a creature within the area would first meaningfully focus visual attention on the caster, it makes a Will save against DC 10 + the caster's Level + ATR + modifiers. On a failed save, the creature's attention passes over the caster in favor of other plausible subjects. Overlook does not make the caster invisible and cannot prevent attention when the caster is the only plausible focus. Creatures affected by Overlook may still perceive consequences caused by the caster. If the caster takes an overt hostile action during an ongoing conflict, Overlook immediately ceases to affect creatures participating in that conflict. A creature that succeeds on its save is unaffected by that casting of Overlook.

While sustained, creatures within 100 m that would meaningfully focus visual attention on the caster must make a Will save. On a failed save, their attention passes over the caster when another plausible focus exists. Overlook does not function when the caster is the only plausible focus and ceases to affect participants in a conflict once the caster takes an overt hostile action.

Inspire alters a willing creature's emotional state, filling it with confidence toward a particular task. When the spell is cast, choose one type of roll, such as attack rolls or a specific skill. The target gains a +1 bonus to rolls of the chosen type for ATR minutes. The choice is made each time Inspire is cast.
Choose one type of roll when Inspire is cast. The willing target gains +1 to rolls of that type for ATR minutes.

Charm alters a creature's emotional disposition toward the caster, causing the target to regard the caster as unusually friendly, familiar, or trustworthy. The target makes a Will save against DC 10 + the caster's Level + ATR + modifiers. 

On a failed save, a sapient creature becomes favorably disposed toward the caster, granting the caster +2 on Diplomacy, Deception, Disguise, and applicable Commerce checks involving that creature. Charm changes disposition rather than knowledge, memory, beliefs, obligations, or training. If a sapient creature succeeds on its Will save, the attempted manipulation instead leaves it distrustful of the caster, imposing a -2 penalty on those same checks against it for ATR minutes. 

On a failed save, a non-sapient creature becomes calm and favorably disposed toward the caster. Ordinary aggression caused by fear, territoriality, predation, or general hostility toward the caster ends, but the creature retains its training, learned rules, protective behavior, and other reasons for acting. Charm grants no general bonus to Animal Handling. Charm ends if the caster takes an overtly hostile action against the target.

On a failed Will save, a sapient target becomes favorably disposed toward the caster, granting +2 to Diplomacy, Deception, Disguise, and applicable Commerce checks involving it. A non-sapient target instead becomes calm and ceases ordinary instinctive aggression toward the caster. Charm ends if the caster takes an overtly hostile action against the target.

Phantom Sound causes one willing or unwitting creature within range to experience a brief simple sound that has no external source. The sound lasts less than one second and may be any simple noise the caster can define, such as a knock, footstep, bell, animal call, creak, or series of brief tones. Phantom Sound creates the auditory experience but does not force the target to believe that the sound is real, identify its source incorrectly, or react to it in any particular way. Once a creature recognizes that a sound it experienced was created by Phantom Sound, it may choose to reject further Phantom Sounds. A creature that is rejecting Phantom Sound cannot be affected by the spell from any caster. It may stop rejecting Phantom Sound at any time. A creature that already knows Phantom Sound is being used against it may reject the spell before experiencing it. Recognition of the spell is not automatic merely because the sound is experienced.

Cause the target to experience one brief simple sound lasting less than one second. Once the target recognizes Phantom Sound, it may reject further Phantom Sounds and cannot be affected again until it chooses to stop rejecting them.

Induce Vertigo disrupts the target's perception of balance and spatial orientation, causing it to experience the world as though physically suffering from vertigo without actually disturbing the inner ear. The target makes a Will save against DC 10 + the caster's Level + ATR + modifiers when the spell is cast. On a failed save, the target gains the Vertigo condition for 1 + ATR of the target's turns. The target does not make additional saves during the duration. Because the effect is perceptual rather than physical, resistance to poisons, diseases, or other physical causes of vertigo does not protect against this spell.
The target makes one Will save when the spell is cast. On a failed save, it gains the Vertigo condition for 1 + ATR of its turns.

Comfort Zone creates a 3 m radius zone centered on one willing creature. While the spell is sustained, willing creatures within the zone perceive the ambient temperature as comfortably warm or cool regardless of the actual temperature. The spell changes only the subjective sensation of temperature. It does not alter the environment, regulate body temperature, prevent dehydration, protect against exposure, or reduce heat or cold damage. Creatures within the zone may therefore feel perfectly comfortable while still suffering the normal physical consequences of extreme heat or cold. The targeted creature serves as the center of the zone, and the zone moves with it. If the target moves more than 100 m from the caster, the spell ends.

Creates a 3 m radius zone centered on the target. Willing creatures within the zone experience the ambient temperature as comfortably warm or cool. This does not change actual temperature or protect against the physical effects of heat or cold.

Phantom Sensation causes one willing or unwitting creature within range to experience a false sensation of smell, taste, or touch. When the spell is cast, choose one of those senses and define a simple sensation for the target to experience for the duration. The sensation may replace or overlay what the target would normally perceive, but it does not alter the physical object, environment, or the target's body. Phantom Sensation cannot create pain, temperature, or effects involving balance or spatial orientation. The caster may accurately reproduce sensations they know or create an invented sensation, but the spell does not provide knowledge of sensations the caster has never experienced or otherwise learned. Once a creature recognizes that its perception is being altered by Phantom Sensation, it may reject the effect, ending the current spell and preventing further Phantom Sensations from affecting it until it chooses to stop rejecting them. A creature that already knows Phantom Sensation is being used against it may reject the spell before experiencing it. Recognition of the spell is not automatic merely because the sensation is experienced.

Cause the target to experience a false smell, taste, or tactile sensation for 1 + ATR minutes. The sensation changes only the target's perception and does not alter physical reality. A target that recognizes Phantom Sensation may reject and end it.

Fear fills the target with supernatural dread directed toward the caster. Fear is an Emotion effect. The target makes a Will save against DC 10 + the caster's Level + ATR + modifiers when the spell is cast. On a failed save, the target becomes Shaken for 1 + ATR of the target's turns. Fear conditions caused by this spell stack with other Fear effects according to the Fear Effects rules. When cast at higher levels, Fear inflicts increasingly severe Fear conditions.

The target makes one Will save when Fear is cast. On a failed save, it becomes Shaken for 1 + ATR of its turns. At cast level 4, Fear instead inflicts Frightened. At cast level 6, it instead inflicts Panicked.

Dampen Emotion suppresses the intensity of the target's emotional experience. While the spell is sustained, all other Emotion-tagged effects affecting the target are suppressed and provide none of their normal mechanical effects. Their durations continue normally and may resume if Dampen Emotion ends before they do. New Emotion effects may still be applied while Dampen Emotion is active, but remain suppressed for as long as the spell continues. Dampen Emotion suppresses beneficial and harmful Emotion effects equally. Ordinary emotions are also substantially muted, though the target retains its memories, knowledge, judgment, relationships, and ability to choose its actions. The caster may target themself or a willing creature without a save. An unwilling creature is affected when the spell is cast, but makes a Will save at the beginning of each of its turns. On a successful save, Dampen Emotion ends for that creature.

Suppress all other Emotion-tagged effects affecting the target while Dampen Emotion is sustained. Self and willing targets receive no save. An unwilling target makes a Will save at the beginning of each turn; success ends the spell.

Phantom Bolt projects a convincing experience of injury or structural damage into a target. Make a ranged attack against one creature within range. On a hit, the target gains 1d6 + ATR Phantom Damage. Phantom Damage does not reduce HP or physically injure the target. It combines with real damage when determining whether the creature becomes incapacitated and remains until rejected according to the Phantom Damage rules.
Deal 1d6 + ATR Phantom Damage on a successful ranged attack.

Phantom Burst projects convincing experiences of injury or structural damage into creatures within a small area. Choose one hex within range; the chosen hex and each adjacent hex are affected. Each creature in the area gains 1d6 + ATR Phantom Damage. Phantom Damage does not reduce HP or physically injure the target. It combines with real damage when determining whether the creature becomes incapacitated and remains until rejected according to the Phantom Damage rules.

When this spell is learned, the caster chooses the appearance of a weapon, such as a sword, dagger, axe, spear, or scythe. This choice has no mechanical effect. When Phantom Weapon is cast, the target perceives the chosen weapon floating nearby and attacking them, though no physical weapon exists and creatures other than the target do not perceive it. Make a melee attack against one creature within range. On a hit, the target gains 1d6 + ATR Phantom Damage. Phantom Damage does not reduce HP or physically injure the target. It combines with real damage when determining whether the creature becomes incapacitated and remains until rejected according to the Phantom Damage rules.
Deal 1d6 + ATR Phantom Damage on a successful melee attack.

Induce Nausea manipulates the target's perception of its own bodily condition, producing an overwhelming sensation of sickness without physically poisoning or injuring it. The target makes a Will save when the spell is cast. On a failure, it gains the Nausea condition for 1 + ATR target turns. At the beginning of each affected turn, the target makes another Will save. On a success, Nausea ends; on a failure, the target loses 1 AP that turn. Nausea does not stack. Additional applications refresh the duration rather than increasing the AP penalty.
On a failed Will save, inflict Nausea. The target loses 1 AP each turn it fails its beginning-of-turn Will save. Nausea does not stack.

Phantom Interface creates a subjective visual interface within the caster's perception, providing immediate access to information the caster already knows, remembers, or could reasonably derive from available observations. The interface may present text, diagrams, numerical estimates, visual markers, reminders, and other convenient representations of information. It can retrieve forgotten or difficult-to-recall knowledge and perform calculations or deductions that the caster could accomplish with sufficient time and attention. The interface does not independently verify information or grant knowledge the caster does not possess or could not reasonably derive. Incorrect memories, mistaken assumptions, and misleading observations may produce incorrect displays. The interface exists only within the caster's perception, requires no Sustain, and remains active for 24 hours unless dispelled.

Immediately retrieve, organize, calculate, and display information already known to or reasonably derivable by the caster. Does not independently verify information or grant new knowledge. Can be dispelled.

Somatic Relief allows the target to reject fabricated bodily distress or suppress the subjective symptoms of genuine physical ailments. Choose Immediate Relief or Sustained Relief when casting. Immediate Relief removes all Phantom Damage and dispels other Somatic-tagged Delusion effects affecting the target. It does not remove the physical causes of genuine ailments or provide lasting relief from them. Sustained Relief suppresses other Somatic-tagged effects and the debilitating subjective symptoms of physical ailments for as long as the spell is maintained. Existing Phantom Damage is removed when Sustained Relief begins, and new Phantom Damage produces no effect while the spell is sustained. Nausea and other applicable Somatic conditions do not impose their normal penalties while suppressed. Poison, disease, physical injuries, and other underlying causes continue normally, including any actual HP damage or physical limitations they produce. Symptoms caused by genuine ailments may return when Sustained Relief ends if their causes remain. Somatic Relief does not restore HP or repair physical damage.

Immediate Relief: Remove all Phantom Damage and dispel other Somatic-tagged Delusion effects. Sustained Relief: Remove existing Phantom Damage and suppress new Phantom Damage, other Somatic-tagged effects, and eligible subjective symptoms of physical ailments while sustained. Does not heal physical damage or remove underlying ailments.

Phantom Image creates one coherent false visual subject within a creature's perception. The caster may alter the apparent appearance of a person, creature, or object, or cause the target to see a person, creature, or object that is not physically present. The image may move and behave appropriately but produces no actual sound, smell, touch, or physical effects. Only the target perceives the image; other creatures see the actual environment. The target receives no initial save merely for seeing the image. If circumstances give the target reason to suspect the image is false, it makes a Will save at the beginning of its next turn and every subsequent turn while the image remains. Recasting Phantom Image does not reset established suspicion. A successful save ends the image. Physically touching the phantom or interacting with a falsely represented appearance disrupts the image immediately. After successfully rejecting or physically disrupting a Phantom Image, the target may reject further Phantom Images from the same caster without a save for 24 hours, but may voluntarily accept them. The spell cannot replace an entire environment or create multiple independent visual subjects.

Create one subjective false visual subject or alter the apparent appearance of an existing subject. No initial save. Suspicion grants a Will save at the beginning of every turn until the image ends. Physical interaction disrupts the image immediately. Successful rejection allows the target to reject further Phantom Images from the same caster for 24 hours.
Willing: up to 24 hours; unwilling: 1 + ATR target turns

Sensory Saturation overwhelms one chosen natural sensory mode within the target's perception, replacing useful distinctions with a uniform or overwhelming subjective signal. Eligible senses include sight, hearing, smell, taste, thermal perception, echolocation, and vibration sense. The spell cannot affect magical senses. Saturating sight inflicts Blinded. Saturating another sense prevents the target from obtaining useful information through that sense, including any Precise Sense it provides. A willing creature receives no save and may retain the effect for up to 24 hours, dismissing it at any time without an action. An unwilling creature receives an initial Will save to negate the spell. On a failure, the chosen sense is saturated for up to 1 + ATR target turns. At the beginning of each affected turn, the creature makes another Will save; success ends the spell. The spell does not physically damage or alter the affected sensory organs.

Saturate one chosen natural sensory mode. Sight saturation inflicts Blinded; other senses cannot provide useful information while saturated. Willing targets may dismiss the effect without an action. Unwilling targets receive an initial Will save and beginning-of-turn Will saves to end the effect.

The target's perception of distance becomes subtly unreliable, causing it to misjudge where its attacks must land. On a failed initial Will save, the target suffers a −1 penalty to attack rolls for every full 10 m of actual distance between itself and the creature or object it attacks. This penalty applies to melee and ranged attacks but does not alter actual distance, movement, attack range, or projectile trajectories. Attacks without attack rolls are unaffected. At the beginning of each affected turn, the target makes another Will save; success ends the spell. The effect otherwise expires after 1 + ATR target turns.
−1 to attack rolls per full 10 m of actual distance to the attack's target. Initial Will save negates; beginning-of-turn Will save ends the effect.

The caster creates one coherent phantom person, creature, or object within a single target's perception. The phantom can appear to move and interact naturally, and the target can see, hear, smell, and feel it. Only the target perceives the phantom; it does not exist externally and cannot exert real force, move objects, support weight, obstruct movement, restrain creatures, or deal damage. Its tactile presence can convincingly simulate approximately 10 kg of apparent resistance. If the target physically interacts with the phantom using force exceeding that threshold, the absence of real resistance becomes unmistakable and the spell ends immediately without a save. The target receives no initial Will save merely for perceiving the phantom. Once reasonable suspicion is established, including through credible warnings from others or contradictory evidence, the target makes a Will save at the beginning of its next turn and each subsequent turn until the spell ends; success rejects the phantom and ends the spell. Recasting does not reset established suspicion. After successfully rejecting or physically exposing a Phantom Presence, the target may reject further Phantom Presences from the same caster for 24 hours without a save, but may voluntarily accept them. The spell ends if the caster ceases sustaining it or the target leaves sustained range.

One multisensory phantom perceived only by the target. Apparent resistance approximately 10 kg; exceeding it through physical interaction dispels the phantom. Suspicion permits beginning-of-turn Will saves to reject it. No real force or damage.

Confidence reinforces a willing creature's trust in its own judgment and ability. For ATR minutes, the target gains a +2 bonus to saving throws against Delusion effects, including subsequent saves to reject them. Confidence does not reveal Delusions or automatically establish suspicion. Additionally, the target adds +2 to the result of each individual damage die it rolls, without exceeding that die's natural maximum. Flat damage bonuses are unaffected. Confidence does not increase attack accuracy or the maximum possible damage of an attack. Confidence is an Emotion-tagged effect.
Confidence gives +2 to saves against Delusion effects. +2 to each individual damage die, capped at that die's natural maximum. Does not automatically reveal Delusions.

Alternate Reality replaces a willing creature's sensory experience with a fully immersive subjective environment. When casting, choose Created Reality or Revisited Reality. Created Reality places the participant in an authored, interactive environment that they experience and explore as themselves. Revisited Reality reconstructs an experience from the participant's own memories, allowing them to revisit events and examine details they may not have consciously noticed at the time. The reconstruction is limited to information retained in the participant's memory and may contain omissions, distortions, or plausible but inaccurate details; the spell does not verify the truth of memories or reveal information the participant never recorded. In either mode, the participant's physical body remains in the real world while their ordinary sensory experience is replaced. They cannot meaningfully perceive their actual surroundings or defend themselves against external threats while immersed. Physical injury, environmental danger, and outside attempts to communicate do not automatically end the experience. The participant may voluntarily leave the Alternate Reality, and the spell ends if the caster ceases sustaining it or the participant leaves sustained range.

Fully immersive subjective reality. Created Reality provides an authored, interactive environment; Revisited Reality reconstructs the participant's own potentially inaccurate memories. The participant cannot meaningfully perceive or defend against threats in the real world while immersed.

Icon of Delusion envelops the caster in an aura of extraordinary mental conviction and mastery over subjective experience. While sustained, the caster's Delusion spells cost 1 less MP, and ATR bonuses and ATR-governed effects of those spells use twice the caster's ATR. Whenever the caster's Delusion spells deal Phantom Damage, they deal an additional 2d6 Phantom Damage. The caster and all allied creatures within the aura gain the benefits of Confidence and Inspire: +2 to saving throws against Delusion effects, +2 to each individual damage die without exceeding that die's natural maximum, and +1 to all rolls and checks rather than a single chosen category. The caster gains DR equal to ATR, bypassed by Phantom Damage. The aura extends to a radius of 2 × ATR meters. Icon of Delusion can be sustained for up to ATR rounds and can be used only once per day.

Delusion spells cost 1 less MP and double ATR for spell effects; +2d6 Phantom Damage; caster and allies in aura gain Confidence and +1 to all rolls and checks from Inspire; caster gains DR equal to ATR, bypassed by Phantom Damage. Once per day.

Summon Lesser Elemental calls a lesser elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. When cast, choose a prime element for which you possess affinity, or a derivative element for which you possess both parent affinities. The summoned elemental remains present while the spell is sustained and disappears when the spell ends. This spell can summon Fire, Wind, Water, Earth, Lightning, Steam, Magma, Ice, Sand, or Mud elementals. It cannot summon Celestial elementals. When this spell is learned, choose one prime elemental affinity you do not already possess and gain that affinity.
Summon one Lesser Elemental of an available element into the target hex.

Guardian Earth Elemental summons a specialized Earth Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Guardian Earth Elemental gains a +4 Natural Armor bonus to AC and 6 additional HP per caster level. Unless otherwise ordered, the elemental seeks to protect the summoner from attack. When this spell is learned, if you do not already possess Earth affinity, you gain Earth affinity.
Summon one Guardian Earth Elemental into the target hex.

Farshot Wind Elemental summons a specialized Wind Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Farshot Wind Elemental doubles the normal range of its Wind Blade and has an expanded critical range with that attack. Unless otherwise ordered, the elemental seeks to maintain distance from enemies while making ranged attacks. When this spell is learned, if you do not already possess Wind affinity, you gain Wind affinity.
Summon one Farshot Wind Elemental into the target hex.

Healing Spring Water Elemental summons a specialized Water Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. Like a normal Water Elemental, it attaches itself to the summoner, shares the summoner's hex, moves with the summoner, and makes its normal attacks against nearby enemies. While attached, the Healing Spring Water Elemental grants Fast Healing 2 to itself and the summoner. When this spell is learned, if you do not already possess Water affinity, you gain Water affinity.
Summon one Healing Spring Water Elemental into the target hex.

Firebloom Elemental summons a specialized Fire Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. Like a normal Fire Elemental, it can make a 2 m ranged flame attack dealing 1d6 Fire damage to one target. Instead of making this attack, the Firebloom Elemental may deal 1d6 Fire damage to every creature in an adjacent hex. If the Firebloom Elemental is destroyed, it deals 1d6 Fire damage to every creature in an adjacent hex. Unless otherwise ordered, the elemental seeks to close with enemies and position itself where its area attacks can affect multiple targets. When this spell is learned, if you do not already possess Fire affinity, you gain Fire affinity.
Summon one Firebloom Elemental into the target hex.

Wisp Crow summons a small, vaguely crow-shaped magical creature with 1 HP into an unoccupied hex within range. The Wisp Crow can fly, manipulate or carry small objects, search for simple categories of objects, and follow straightforward concrete commands. Its intelligence is limited: it can understand commands such as "push that button," "bring me a ring," or "find food," but cannot independently solve complex problems or reliably interpret highly specific requests. Broad requests are answered according to the crow's own simple understanding and may produce unexpected results. Only one Wisp Crow summoned by this spell may exist at a time.
Summon one Wisp Crow into the target hex.

Caustic Mire Elemental summons a specialized Mud Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Caustic Mire Elemental has exceptionally high HP and an acidic body. Physical attacks that strike the elemental expose the attacker to its caustic substance, and the elemental can splash acid against nearby creatures. Unless otherwise ordered, it seeks to interpose itself between the summoner and hostile creatures and impair the movement of enemies within its reach.
Summon one Caustic Mire Elemental into the target hex.

Sandveil Elemental summons a specialized Sand Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Sandveil Elemental is a Symbiote. Like a normal Sand Elemental, it attaches itself to the summoner, shares the summoner's hex, moves with the summoner, and makes its normal attacks against nearby enemies. While attached, the Sandveil Elemental grants the summoner +4 AC against ranged attacks and DR 4 against damage from ranged attacks by redirecting, slowing, or dissipating incoming attacks. These defenses provide no benefit against melee attacks.
Summon one Sandveil Elemental into the target hex.

Blizzard Elemental summons a specialized Ice Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. Instead of the normal Ice Elemental's ranged icicle attack, the Blizzard Elemental controls a persistent blizzard occupying one hex and every adjacent hex. Creatures exposed to the blizzard take its Cold damage no more than once per turn. The Blizzard Elemental may spend 1 AP to move the blizzard up to 10 m. Unless otherwise ordered, it seeks to place the blizzard over distant groups of enemies, or a distant enemy if no group is available, while avoiding allies.
Summon one Blizzard Elemental into the target hex.

Volcano Elemental summons a specialized Magma Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Volcano Elemental retains the normal Magma Elemental's extremely powerful close-range attack and can also launch a volcanic eruption at a distant area. Creatures caught in the eruption make a DEX save against its damage. The eruption is comparatively easy to avoid, making the Volcano Elemental most effective against enemies whose movement has been restricted.
Summon one Volcano Elemental into the target hex.

Sauna Elemental summons a specialized Steam Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. Like a normal Steam Elemental, it affects every adjacent hex with its steam. Enemies in those hexes take the Steam Elemental's normal damage, while allies in those hexes are healed instead of harmed. Unless otherwise ordered, the Sauna Elemental seeks to position itself so that its steam affects as many battlefield participants as possible.
Summon one Sauna Elemental into the target hex.

Arcstep Elemental summons a specialized Lightning Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Arcstep Elemental retains the normal Lightning Elemental's ranged lightning attack, including its ability to link to adjacent enemies, and may move itself to the targeted hex after resolving that attack. The Arcstep Elemental also has additional RP and may spend 1 RP when struck to move away, dealing a small amount of Lightning damage to creatures in hexes it passes through. Unless otherwise ordered, the Arcstep Elemental seeks to cross as much of the battlefield as possible, preferentially attacking distant targets and using its movement to relocate far from its current position.
Summon one Arcstep Elemental into the target hex.

Aether Elemental summons a versatile Aether Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Aether Elemental is a true generalist, capable of melee and ranged attacks, good movement, and solid durability. It possesses above-animal intelligence and can adapt its behavior to changing circumstances. The summoner shares a telepathic bond with the elemental and may issue direct commands to it without spending AP. Unless otherwise ordered, the Aether Elemental uses its abilities as it judges most useful to assist the summoner.
Summon one Aether Elemental into the target hex.

Life Elemental summons a Life Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Life Elemental is the most healer-focused of the elementals. It is capable of using Restoration magic such as Mend Flesh and Healing Bolt to heal living creatures, though it remains less effective as a healer than a dedicated Restoration mage. It can also make ranged attacks of Life energy against living creatures, causing rapid temporary mutations that deal damage. Unless otherwise ordered, the Life Elemental prioritizes healing injured allies and uses its ranged Life attack when no ally requires healing.
Summon one Life Elemental into the target hex.

Light Elemental summons a Light Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Light Elemental is a fragile but versatile celestial combatant. It can make ranged attacks of Light that deal low but very reliable damage, denying enemies their DEX or evasion bonuses to AC. It can also illuminate creatures or objects, cause targets to glow, inflict blindness at range, and wield a high-damage melee weapon of solid Light. Unless otherwise ordered, the Light Elemental maintains distance and uses its ranged attacks and utility abilities, resorting to melee against nearby enemies or when directed to close.
Summon one Light Elemental into the target hex.

Void Elemental summons a Void Elemental into an unoccupied hex within range. The Void Elemental is a control-focused celestial summon. It can create a gravitational field occupying one hex and every adjacent hex, reducing the movement speed of creatures within the field and depriving them of their DEX or evasion bonuses to AC. It also has a ranged Void attack that deals modest damage. The Void Elemental can reposition combatants through spatial manipulation, but swapping the positions of two creatures requires a direct command from the summoner. Unless otherwise ordered, the Void Elemental uses its gravitational field to disrupt groups of enemies and makes ranged attacks against disadvantaged targets.
Summon one Void Elemental into the target hex.

Cinder Toss creates a small orb of flame that the caster hurls at a creature within range. On impact, the orb bursts into flame, dealing fire damage and potentially igniting flammable materials. This entry represents the Fire form of the spell; other elemental forms may use different attack or interaction rules.
Damage increases to 1d8 + ATR; range increases to 20 m.
Damage increases to 2d6 + ATR; range increases to 30 m.
Damage increases to 2d12 + ATR; range increases to 40 m.
Damage increases to 3d10 + ATR; gain +10 to the attack roll.

Fire Bolt is an energy-based expression of Elemental Bolt. The caster manifests a projectile of elemental fire and launches it at a creature within range. On impact, the fire may spread to a second creature adjacent to the original target.

Make a ranged attack against one creature within range. On a successful hit, deal 1d4 + ATR fire damage. The caster may select one different creature adjacent to the original target. That creature must succeed on a Reflex save or take 1d4 + ATR fire damage. A successful save negates the secondary damage. The secondary effect cannot spread further.

Earth Bolt is a matter-based expression of Elemental Bolt. The caster manifests a dense projectile of elemental earth and launches it at a creature within range. The projectile delivers a concentrated physical impact before dissipating shortly afterward.
Make a ranged attack against one creature within range. On a successful hit, deal 1d6 + 2*ATR earth damage.

Wind Bolt is a matter-based expression of Elemental Bolt. The caster manifests a concentrated projectile of compressed air and launches it at a creature within range. The projectile travels considerably farther than most elemental bolts, striking its target with a sudden impact before dissipating.
Make a ranged attack against one creature within range. On a successful hit, deal 1d10 wind damage.

Water Bolt is a matter-based expression of Elemental Bolt. The caster manifests a concentrated projectile of elemental water and launches it at a creature within range. Upon striking its target, the water leaves behind a persistent elemental Wisp that continues attacking the creature until destroyed.

Make a ranged attack against one creature within range. On a successful hit, deal 1d4 + ATR water damage and attach one Water Wisp to the target. The Wisp follows the standard Wisp rules, dealing 1d4 water damage at the start of the affected creature's turn until destroyed or severed.

Elemental Bolt is a fundamental offensive Evocation spell that manifests and launches a projectile of elemental matter or energy. Learning Elemental Bolt grants access to its Fire, Wind, Water, and Earth expressions for which the caster possesses affinity. When learned, the caster may gain one prime elemental affinity they are otherwise eligible to possess. Each expression has its own damage, range, secondary effects, and upgrades while sharing the spell's casting costs. Additional prime expressions become available automatically as the caster acquires their corresponding affinities.

Make one ranged attack against a creature within range using an available prime elemental expression. Apply the damage and any secondary effects specified by that expression. The spell requires no saving throw unless the selected expression specifies otherwise. All expressions share the casting costs of Elemental Bolt.

Steam Bolt is a matter-based expression of Elemental Bolt. The caster manifests a projectile of superheated steam and launches it at a hex within range. On impact, the projectile bursts into a brief cloud of steam that fills the targeted hex before dissipating.

Select one hex within range and make a ranged attack against that hex. On a successful hit, the projectile bursts into a brief cloud of superheated steam, dealing 1d6 steam damage to anything occupying that hex. The cloud dissipates immediately afterward.

Lightning Bolt is an energy-based expression of Elemental Bolt requiring Fire and Wind affinity. The caster manifests a concentrated projectile of lightning and launches it along a straight trajectory. Each successful strike allows the projectile to manifest again beyond the creature struck, continuing along the same trajectory until it misses, reaches three successful hits, or reaches its maximum range.

Launch a projectile of lightning along a straight line and make a ranged attack against the first creature in its path. On a successful hit, deal 1d4 + ATR lightning damage. The projectile then manifests again beyond the struck creature and continues along the same line, making a new ranged attack against the next creature in its path. Each successful hit allows another attack, up to a maximum of three creatures struck. A missed attack ends the spell. The projectile affects allies and enemies alike, and its total range cannot exceed 75 m.

Magma Bolt is a matter-based expression of Elemental Bolt requiring Fire and Earth affinity. The caster manifests a projectile of molten elemental matter and launches it at a creature within range. On impact, the projectile delivers concentrated damage and may scatter molten material onto an adjacent creature, attaching a persistent Magma Wisp.

Make a ranged attack against one creature within range. On a successful hit, deal 1d6 + ATR magma damage. The caster may then attach one Magma Wisp to a different creature adjacent to the original target. The Wisp follows the standard Wisp rules, dealing 1d4 magma damage at the start of the affected creature's turn until destroyed or severed.

Sand Bolt is a matter-based expression of Elemental Bolt requiring Wind and Earth affinity. The caster manifests a stream of high-velocity abrasive particles and directs them at a creature within range. Rather than relying on a single powerful strike, Sand Bolt attacks through a rapid series of small impacts.
Make six ranged attack rolls against one creature within range. Each successful hit deals 1 sand damage. Sand Bolt receives no ATR bonus to damage. Resolve each hit separately.

Ice Bolt is a matter-based expression of Elemental Bolt requiring Wind and Water affinity. The caster manifests a projectile of elemental ice and launches it at a creature within range. Rather than dealing immediate damage, the projectile leaves two persistent Ice Wisps attached to the target, forcing the creature to endure their effects or expend actions removing them.

Make a ranged attack against one creature within range. On a successful hit, deal no immediate damage and attach two Ice Wisps to the target. Each Wisp follows the standard Wisp rules, independently dealing 1d4 ice damage at the start of the affected creature's turn until destroyed or severed.

Mud Bolt is a matter-based expression of Elemental Bolt requiring Water and Earth affinity. The caster manifests a dense projectile of elemental mud and launches it at a creature within range. On impact, the mud deals damage, adheres to the target, and rapidly hardens, progressively restricting movement and coordination as additional layers accumulate.

Make a ranged attack against one creature within range. On a successful hit, deal 1d6 + ATR mud damage and apply one stack of Covered in Mud. Add Mud HP equal to the damage dealt. Covered in Mud persists for ATR rounds. Additional applications add another stack, add their damage to the target's Mud HP, and reset the duration of all existing Covered in Mud stacks.

Elemental Burst is a fundamental area Evocation spell that manifests an elemental explosion at a targeted hex. Learning Elemental Burst may grant the caster one prime elemental affinity they are otherwise eligible to possess. The caster may use any Burst expression for which they possess the required affinity or affinities, with each expression modifying the spell's standard area, range, damage, or secondary effects.

Target one hex within range and make the required tile-targeting attack. On a successful hit, the Burst affects a standard 4-hex area and deals 1d4 + ATR damage of the selected elemental expression. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Individual elemental expressions may modify the spell's damage, range, area, or additional effects.

Fire Burst is an explosive Fire Evocation that manifests at a targeted hex and rapidly expands outward. Fire's natural tendency to spread allows the spell to affect a larger area than a standard Elemental Burst.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Fire Burst explodes across the targeted hex and all six adjacent hexes. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Deal 1d4 + ATR fire damage to affected creatures that do not successfully evade the burst.

Earth Burst is a concentrated Earth Evocation that manifests at a targeted hex and erupts through a compact area. Earth's tendency toward concentrated force reduces the spell's affected area compared with a standard Elemental Burst.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Earth Burst erupts across a concentrated 3-hex area. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Deal 1d4 + 2xATR earth damage to affected creatures that do not successfully evade the burst.

Wind Burst is a ranged Wind Evocation that manifests at a targeted hex and erupts across a compact area. Wind's emphasis on speed and range allows this expression to travel farther than a standard Elemental Burst, while its damage is determined entirely by the force and variability of the manifested air rather than the caster's ATR.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Wind Burst erupts across a standard 4-hex area. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Deal 1d10 wind damage to affected creatures that do not successfully evade the burst.

Water Burst is a persistent Water Evocation that manifests at a targeted hex and erupts across a compact area. Creatures struck by the burst are marked by lingering elemental water that remains attached after the initial impact.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Water Burst erupts across a standard 4-hex area. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Deal 1d4 + ATR water damage to affected creatures that do not successfully evade the burst. Each creature damaged by Water Burst gains one Water Wisp.
3 hexes initially; expands one hex outward

Steam Burst is a delayed area Evocation that manifests a concentrated blast of scalding steam before rapidly spreading across the surrounding battlefield. Unlike Fire, which reaches a broad area immediately, Steam begins in a compact area and expands one round later.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Steam Burst affects a 3-hex area and deals 1d6 steam damage to affected creatures. Creatures may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. One round later, the steam expands into every hex adjacent to the original affected area. The entire expanded area deals 1d6 steam damage, with no ATR bonus, and creatures may again spend RP to make a DEX save. The spell then ends.
50 m from targeted hex; maximum 3 creatures

Lightning Burst is a long-ranged Lightning Evocation that strikes a targeted hex before discharging toward nearby creatures. Rather than filling a conventional area, the electrical burst seeks the three creatures closest to its point of impact, allowing Lightning to threaten creatures across an exceptionally large area while making positioning around the targeted hex dangerous to allies and enemies alike.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, identify the three closest creatures within 50 m of the targeted hex when the spell lands. Those creatures become the targets of the burst. If more creatures are tied for the remaining target positions than there are positions available, randomly determine which tied creatures are targeted. Once determined, the targets do not change. Each targeted creature may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Deal 1d4 + ATR lightning damage to each targeted creature that does not successfully evade the burst.

Magma Burst is a concentrated Magma Evocation that erupts across a compact area before breaking into persistent fragments of elemental magma. The spell combines Earth's concentrated force with Fire's tendency to spread, rewarding careful placement that limits how many creatures can receive the resulting Magma Wisps.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Magma Burst erupts across a concentrated 3-hex area. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Deal 1d6 + ATR magma damage to affected creatures that do not successfully evade the burst. After resolving the damage, create one Magma Wisp for each hex in the affected area and evenly distribute those Wisps among creatures damaged by the Burst. A creature may receive multiple Wisps. If only one creature was damaged by the Burst, all Wisps attach to that creature.

Sand Burst is an area Sand Evocation that fills a compact region with a dense barrage of high-velocity elemental sand. Rather than resolving separate attacks against each creature, the spell produces one shared pattern of six attack rolls that every creature in the affected area must withstand according to its own AC.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Sand Burst affects a standard 4-hex area. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. After RP movement is resolved, roll six ranged attack rolls simultaneously. Every creature remaining in the affected area compares those same six attack results against its own AC and takes 1 sand damage for each attack that hits. Sand Burst gains no ATR damage bonus.

Ice Burst is a persistent Ice Evocation that erupts across a compact area and coats affected creatures in clinging elemental ice. Rather than dealing immediate damage, the spell leaves behind multiple Ice Wisps that continue threatening and hindering those caught in the burst.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Ice Burst affects a standard 4-hex area. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Each creature that does not successfully evade the burst gains 2 Ice Wisps. Ice Burst deals no immediate damage.

Mud Burst is a persistent Mud Evocation that erupts across a compact area, striking creatures with dense elemental mud that adheres to them and rapidly hardens. Creatures repeatedly exposed to the effect accumulate additional layers of mud, progressively restricting their movement and coordination.

Target one hex within range. On a successful tile-targeting attack, Mud Burst affects a standard 4-hex area. Creatures within the affected area may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Burst rules. Deal 1d6 + ATR mud damage to each creature that does not successfully evade the burst and apply one stack of Covered in Mud. Each affected creature gains Mud HP equal to the damage dealt to it. Covered in Mud persists for ATR rounds. Additional applications add another stack, add their damage to that creature's Mud HP, and reset the duration of all existing Covered in Mud stacks.

Fire Blast is a close-range Fire Evocation that projects an explosive cone of flame outward from the caster. Fire's tendency to spread extends the spell one rank farther than a standard Elemental Blast, allowing it to engulf a substantially larger area at the cost of requiring the caster to fight at close range.

Choose either legal 3 m cone orientation originating from the caster. Every creature within the affected hexes may spend RP to make a DEX save as permitted by the standard Blast rules. Deal 1d4 fire damage to each creature that does not successfully evade the blast. Fire Blast does not distinguish between allies and enemies.
